words.gloss: things that ought to be done
that which is destined to survive

literal: The wealth of him who, without doing things that ought to be done, is miserly, without any way of surviving, will perish.
translation: The wealth of a miserly person, who fails to perform the duties he ought to do, will surely perish without any chance of survival.
modern: செய்ய வேண்டிய கடமைகளைச் செய்யாமல் கஞ்சத்தனமாக வாழ்பவனுடைய செல்வம், தப்பிப் பிழைக்கும் வழியின்றி அழிந்துவிடும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the twin vices of neglecting one's duties and hoarding wealth out of miserliness. The word 'செயற்பால' refers to actions or duties that are fit and necessary to be performed, such as charity or civic duties. 'இவறியான்' describes a miser who hoards wealth instead of spending it on these necessary duties. The poet states that the wealth of such a person has no way of escaping ('உயற்பாலது அன்றி') and is destined to be completely ruined ('கெடும்').
